files.migration_notes:
Convert static HTML to Vite entry point. Replace jQuery script tag with React root div (e.g.,
) and module script type. Move inline scripts to React components. Update asset references to Vite public path (e.g., /logo.png). Ensure environment variables use VITE_ prefix.

Global styles can be imported in main.jsx. Consider CSS Modules for component-scoped styles (e.g., TaskItem.module.css). Keep existing classes but avoid global selectors; use className in JSX. Remove box-sizing typo (border-box -> border-box).

Major jQuery patterns to convert:
1. $(document).ready -> useEffect with empty deps or component mount.
2. Global selectors ($('#task-list'), $('#stats')) -> React state and refs.
3. DOM manipulation (append, remove, toggleClass, hide/show) -> declarative rendering via state arrays.
4. Event delegation ($('#task-list').on('click', '.delete-btn')) -> onClick handlers on each TaskItem.
5. Checkbox change -> controlled component with onChange updating task completion.
6. Filter toggle (showingCompletedOnly) -> state filter and derived visibleTasks.
7. AJAX load -> useEffect with fetch, set initial tasks state.
8. Data attributes (li.data('taskId')) -> task objects with id property.
9. updateStats -> computed from tasks state.
10. $.trim -> String.trim().
Structure: Single App component with state { tasks: [], showCompletedOnly: false }. Sub-components: TaskInput, TaskList, TaskItem, Stats, Controls. Use functional components and hooks.

overall_notes: Migration strategy: Set up Vite React project, migrate HTML to entry point, move CSS to src, rewrite app.js as React component with hooks. Risks: jQuery's imperative DOM mutations vs React's declarative rendering; ensure state updates trigger re-renders correctly. Event delegation replaced by per-item handlers. AJAX migration to fetch with error handling. Global variable showingCompletedOnly becomes component state. Use Vite environment variables (VITE_) if needed. Test each feature incrementally. Consider TypeScript for better maintainability.
